purpose: Role skill of the Readymerce paid-ads system that directs and produces cinematic AI drama ads (short films, 25 to 120 s, vertical 9:16) from story through screenplay, treatment, shot list, set bible and frames, animatic, multi-model video generation, sound, music, edit, grade, captions, loudness and a scored film test. The hub (readymerce-ads-machine) owns research and hard gates; Hook Lab owns the hook; Script Lab gates the words; this skill owns the film. Its exceptions table (0b, X1 and X3 to X10) relaxes hub Section G for drama only.

phases.name: Module 0 research and the concept card (sections 0, 2, 3)
phases.does: Runs hub Module 0 (brief A1, research and VOC A2, concept memo A3, Voice Card B1, Conviction Map B2). Uses the 8-question picker to choose a template (T1 to T13), then fills every concept-card field: template, hero, want, outside and inside problem, reacting person, dramatic question, stakes and clock, device, scene turns, product arc (plant, echo, fire), motif, failed fixes, cause line, payoff on a face, emotional shape, identity and button, comment test. Then writes a 6 to 8 line 'because of that' beat list.
phases.gate: Every field is filled. Kill the concept if the conflict could happen with any product, nobody but the hero is in the scene, it fails the no-logo test, nothing changes, or it fails the comment test. Batch rules: no two ads share template and angle, at least 2 templates per concept, T6 and T9 never lead a first test.
phases.human_checkpoint: Stop only if a brand fact the script needs is missing (0.6). No numbered GATE.
phases.tools_models: readymerce-ads-machine (Module 0); Appendix B and C as structural models

phases.name: Hook Lab, drama-adapted (7.4, X7, X8)
phases.does: Runs readymerce-hook-lab. The visual hook is the opening shot sequence (7.2 opening recipe), graded on concept frames. The spoken hook is the first line wherever it lands inside 4 s. The text channel is optional and off by default. Writes 3 hook variants that change only the first 3 to 4 s.
phases.gate: Hook Lab gates still apply: buyer lock by 2 s sound-off, one claim, problem readable by 2 s, a seam into the next beat, an open question at 10 s, no product or brand in the first 3 s. X8: first line by 1.5 s by default (up to 4.0 s only after a strong readable action), a real sound by 0.3 s, a story event by 1.0 s.

phases.name: Screenplay and the Script Lab gate (section 5)
phases.does: Script Lab WRITE with the drama adapter: SCENE headers, V# visual beats, S# sound cues, L# lines with gap codes (S 0.15 s, B 0.4 s, H 0.8 s). Dialogue rules (core lines 3 to 10 words, none over 17, one turn up to 25; doubter questions of 6 words or fewer). Adds 12 drama checks. Runs two cold reads by fresh agents: a listen read (spoken lines only) and a picture read (V-beats and S-cues only).
phases.gate: Release at 85 or more with no critical fail. Up to 3 rewrite loops, then the user decides. Both cold reads pass (X10). The short tier (C45) is written and gated on its own, never trimmed from the S90.
phases.human_checkpoint: The user decides after 3 failed rewrite loops.
phases.tools_models: readymerce-script-lab (WRITE, GRADE, FIX); fresh agents for the cold reads

phases.name: Voices, the scene master and the transcript check (section 10)
phases.does: Casts one locked ElevenLabs voice per character (eleven_v3 or eleven_v4) with one audio tag per line and auditions 3 to 4 takes. Rejects takes with no energy above 8 kHz, a wrong word or a rushed line. Builds the scene master: turn gaps 0.08 to 0.3 s, occasional 0.1 to 0.2 s overlaps, planned silences at animatic length, and a line table. Transcribes the master. Cuts per-character packed stems with listening gaps (0.8 to 3 s), padded to a whole second (4 to 15 s) with a 0.3 s head handle, and converts them to MP3.
phases.gate: Every wrong word is fixed before any video. The scene master sets the real timing for everything after it.
phases.tools_models: ElevenLabs creative_generate_speech (eleven_v3 / eleven_v4); Scribe or faster-whisper

phases.name: Director's treatment (section 6)
phases.does: Writes a one-page treatment: logline, tone, visual arc, light plan per scene (warm 2700 to 3200K practicals vs cool 5600K+; contrast 4:1, 8:1 at the low point; the light change at the turn), palette per act, face-light patterns, lens package, camera philosophy, performance notes, texture (24 fps, 35mm grain), sound world, music concept, caption style.
phases.gate: One page per ad, included in the deliverable.

phases.name: Floor plans and the set bible (8.1, 8.2)
phases.does: Makes casting cards and set cards using the podcast reference pipeline (Pinterest sourcing, 8-point score, likeness rule). Per setting it builds: a floor plan with the 180-degree line; a 16:9 location master; character sheets made only from the master; anchor lines; a prop and wardrobe lock; a lighting bible; coverage plates; a hero still.
phases.gate: Identity rule: a person's identity comes only from the location master plus their sheet. No frame-from-frame chains, except one match-on-action hop checked against the sheet.
phases.tools_models: GPT Image 2 at 2K (location master); GPT Image 2 or Nano Banana Pro (sheets); 3D Jutsu location-new-angles or an image model (coverage plates); readymerce-podcast-ads v5.0 sections 3 to 5

phases.name: The shot list, timed on the scene master (7.1 to 7.7)
phases.does: One row per shot with 17 columns: time, beat, job, size, angle, lens, motivated move, timed blocking, eyeline and screen side, light, continuity state, line and sound, lip-sync, model route, frames, takes. Applies the tension ladder, turn marking, power angles, the opening recipe, dialogue coverage and vertical rules. Writes a retention map with one line per 10 s window.
phases.gate: 15 hard rules. Examples: no adjacent same size and angle; 50% or more moving shots, each motivated; S90 size mix; listener on screen 35 to 50%; visible lip-sync on 60% of lines or fewer; geography by 8 s; adjacent shot lengths differ by 25% or more; 30-degree rule; something changes every 2 to 4 s (every 1 to 1.5 s in the first 5 s); continuity state column filled; the product's person never faces the lens; runtime inside the tier (S90 at 100 s or less). Retention rules 7.7: proof on screen at each claim line, a payoff insert held 1.5 to 2.5 s, no 10 s window without a new event. A window with nothing new is redesigned.

phases.name: Shot frames (storyboard) and frame QA (8.3)
phases.does: One 9:16 start frame per shot, made from the location master, character sheets and coverage plate. Each prompt carries size, angle, lens, positions and eyelines, world-source light, time of day, continuity state, and 'no text'. Composition-bleed rule: inserts and close-ups get a crop of the master or no set image. An end frame is made when a move or reveal must land. Inserts use the real product image.
phases.gate: Frame QA on every frame: same person as the sheet, right screen side and eyeline, right light source, prop in the right hand, no extra fingers, nothing important in the bottom 35%, words spelled exactly, the size asked for, nobody extra in frame, continuity state, the product's person not facing the lens, adjacent frames of the same person visibly different. A crossed eyeline is regenerated, not flipped.
phases.tools_models: Image model with references (GPT Image 2 / Nano Banana Pro per 8.2)

phases.name: Animatic gate (section 9)
phases.does: Lays shot frames on the voice master at real timing, with temp sound cues, music-map markers and still pushes where the shot list has a move. Renders a low-res MP4 plus a labelled frame sheet (one frame per shot with number, time and line). Says plainly that it is still frames.
phases.gate: Reviewed against the 7.6 rules, the opening recipe, the tension ladder, the 35 to 50% listener share, turn marking, shot-length variety and the vertical safe band. Watched once on mute (story clear) and once with eyes closed (selling facts clear).
phases.human_checkpoint: The only creative human gate: if the user is present, send the animatic and the cost preflight and wait for 'go' or notes. If the user is away, state which reading was taken and continue. (Not numbered as GATE n.)

phases.name: Cost preflight (11.5)
phases.does: Prices every model with generate_video get_cost: true and checks balance right before submitting. Plans S90 at about 3,000 to 4,500 credits and C45 at about 1,500 to 2,500, including drafts and a 30% contingency. On a new account or model mix, runs a 3-shot pilot first.
phases.gate: The balance or budget covers the whole ad, or the scope is agreed first (shoot the C45 first, cut a setting, or move inserts to stills).
phases.human_checkpoint: Stop and agree the scope with the user if the budget cannot cover the whole ad.

phases.name: Generation: drafts, then finals, then Sync 3 passes (11.1 to 11.5)
phases.does: Routes each shot by type with the routing card. One prompt per row in a fixed order: format, reference jobs, camera, size, angle, subject anchor, action timeline, setting layers, light, palette, texture, dialogue or silent, then 2 to 5 locks and negatives. Drafts at cheap tiers and finalizes only winners. Takes per shot follow the takes table.
phases.gate: Model limits respected: H3 never gets audio_references with start/end images; H3 clip = stem + 1 s; silent shots go to Kling; veo3_1 takes a start frame only; Kling end frame must match wardrobe. On a preset recommendation, resubmit with declined_preset_id. One camera move per clip (two compatible at most).
phases.human_checkpoint: Stop if every route for a needed shot has failed twice.
phases.tools_models: minimax_h3 (2K), minimax_h3_max, kling3_0, kling_o3_*, seedance_2_5, cinematic_studio_video_4_0 / 3_5, veo3_1 / veo3_1_lite, gemini_omni_flash_1_1, kling_video_edit, sync_so (Sync Lipsync 3), ElevenLabs audio_isolation, 3D Jutsu

phases.name: Per-take QA (11.6)
phases.does: Makes a frame sheet per clip: one frame every 0.5 s for clips under 6 s, else every 1 s, plus the first and last frames. Lip-synced clips: cross-correlates clip audio with the stem, measures the lag, and transcribes. Picks and logs the usable window (best 1.5 to 4 s), trims 4 to 10 warm-up and tail frames, and keeps a generation log (shot, model, takes, kept seconds, credits).
phases.gate: Same face as the sheet, no morphing hands or props, eyeline and screen side kept, move obeyed, no text artifacts, nothing frozen. Retake when correlation is under about 0.5 with no clear lag, or a word is wrong. Edit in-point = handle + measured lag.

phases.name: Rough cut on the scene master, then picture lock (section 14)
phases.does: Cuts for emotion first (Murch). Rhythm: 2 to 4 shots of 0.8 to 1.5 s in the first 3 s, 2 to 3 s average in the body, accelerating 15 to 30% per beat into the turn, then one held shot of 3 to 6 s. J/L cuts on half or more of dialogue cuts. An insert every 3 to 4 dialogue cuts. 70 to 90% of cuts land on an audio event. Fixed ending sequence. All native clip audio stripped. ffmpeg assembly from a cut map.
phases.gate: No same-framing cuts on the same person (14.9b): a full size step or 30 degrees, re-checked after every edit change.
phases.tools_models: ffmpeg in the Higgs sandbox (nohup, polled in calls under 60 s)

phases.name: Score the locked cut (section 13)
phases.does: Draws a cue sheet (entry, drop, re-entry, swell, stinger, end). Route (a): eleven_video_to_music_v1 on a 540x960 proxy of the locked cut, 3 to 4 takes. Route (b): eleven_music_v2_5 composition plan with sections matched to the cue sheet, 3 to 4 variations each. Edits music on bar lines.
phases.gate: Entry where tension builds (default 0:02 to 0:08). Only a low tension bed under the hook, 20 dB or more under dialogue. Drop 0.5 to 2 s before the key line. 2 to 4 sync points. Music 10 to 18 dB under the voice. No accidental dropout. Final chord on the end card.
phases.human_checkpoint: Tell the user which generated-clip music was kept and why.
phases.tools_models: ElevenLabs creative_create_flow, creative_create_asset_upload / creative_finalize_asset_upload (needed for route a), creative_generate_in_flow (music, video-to-music), creative_get_flow_run_status

phases.name: Sound design (section 12)
phases.does: Builds D/M/E stems. One continuous ambience bed per location (2 to 3 layers, 20 to 30 s loops) via eleven_text_to_sound_v2, with duration_seconds set explicitly because the sfx node defaults to about 2 s. Adds foley on every touch, hard effects, sparing designed sound, 1 to 2 silences of 1 to 3 s, 2 to 3 off-screen sounds per scene, and matched room reverb.
phases.gate: Featured foley peaks 3 to 6 dB under dialogue peaks; touch foley 10 to 16 dB under. Print a per-event peak table and a stem RMS table. Featured effects more than 8 dB under, or touch effects more than 18 dB under, get raised. Never white or pink noise as room tone.
phases.tools_models: ElevenLabs creative_generate_in_flow (node sfx, eleven_text_to_sound_v2), creative_update_node / creative_add_flow_node, creative_run_flow_nodes

phases.name: Upscale (15.1)
phases.does: After picture lock, upscales only the kept window plus 12 frames of handle on each side, to 1080x1920, with moderate noise reduction, moderate to high detail recovery and low grain (15 to 20 of 100).
phases.gate: Warped faces are regenerated, not fixed.

phases.name: Grade and grain (15.3)
phases.does: Normalizes each clip, applies one film look per act at 60 to 80%, matches every shot to the hero still (skin first), adds a 0.3 to 0.6 px blur and 35mm grain at 8 to 15% on every shot, and deflickers.
phases.gate: Phone shadow floor: an average frame luma under about 0.10 (25 of 255), or a lit face under about 0.25, gets lifted.
phases.tools_models: ffmpeg / LUT (Kodak 2383 or Fuji 3510 style), video_deflicker

phases.name: Mix and loudness (15.5)
phases.does: Two-pass loudnorm. Dialogue at -16 to -12 LUFS short-term. Music ducked 6 to 12 dB under lines. Ambience 15 to 25 dB under. Foley 10 to 20 dB under during lines. Hard effects 6 to 15 dB under. Checked on a phone speaker.
phases.gate: -14 LUFS integrated (-15 to -13), true peak -1 dBTP or lower, LRA 6 to 11 LU, short-term never above about -9 LUFS.

phases.name: Captions (15.4)
phases.does: Clean sans or serif with a soft shadow, no box, sentence case. 1 to 4 words per card, white, 80 to 100 px at 1080x1920. 1 to 2 keywords per ad in warm yellow. Placed 55 to 62% down, word-matched to the master.
phases.gate: Never over a face, a key prop or readable in-frame text. No captions over the silent opening. Supers follow X7.

phases.name: Export (15.6)
phases.does: H.264 high profile, 1080x1920, 24 fps, AAC 48 kHz at 192 kbps or more, faststart. Uploads to Higgs (media upload, PUT, confirm) for a link.
phases.gate: Spec met

phases.name: Film-test QA and the score card (section 16)
phases.does: Runs on the rendered file: a frame sheet at 1 frame per second plus every cut's first and last frame; shot, opening, story, sound and music audits; a transcript of the final file; loudness and gap tables; a facts check; two watches (mute, eyes closed); the film test; a continuity audit plus an automatic jump-cut scan (90x160 grey correlation, pairs above about 0.6 reviewed); a retention audit; the 100-point score card.
phases.gate: Release at 85 or more. Below 85, fix the lowest areas and re-render. Never deliver with a known failure. Score areas: Hook 15, Story 15, Picture 10, Continuity 10, Pacing and retention 15, Proof and payoff 10, Sound and music 10, Captions 5, Ending and CTA 10.
phases.human_checkpoint: Tell the user the score and what was fixed. For high-stakes work only, a fresh agent runs checks 2 to 6.

phases.name: Deliver, series and test plan (17, 18)
phases.does: Delivers the package: concept card, hook stacks, screenplay and both cold reads, short tier, treatment, set bible, shot list, frame sheet, animatic, voices, stem map, prompts, generation log, cue sheet, cut map, the ad plus 3 hook variants, primary text, headline, credits against preflight, QA tables. Primary text is 80 to 150 words; headline is 8 words or fewer. Launches the story tier and short tier as separate ads.
phases.gate: After about 1,000 impressions per ad: hook rate floor 30% (target 40%); hold rate floor 25% (target 35%). Judged on new-customer cost at ad-set level over 7 to 14 days.

story_structures.name: The result causes trouble
story_structures.shape: The hero's visible change → an official or stranger refuses to believe she is the person in the old photo → roll call of failed fixes → the product carried in as the price of proof → the doubter converts → button
story_structures.organic_fit: An Albanian workshop owner who used to beg for jobs is now booked out. A supplier or old friend refuses to believe it is the same shop and asks what changed. The reveal is the mechanism (one specific promise in his posts instead of 'cilësi'), not the agency's price. CTA: 'save this' or 'comment HOW for the breakdown'. Needs a documented client result (hub B15d).

story_structures.name: Someone else notices first
story_structures.shape: A partner, kid or stranger spots the problem before the hero admits it → private embarrassment (only after 3 s) → a peer who 'had that happen' names the fix → payoff on the hero's face
story_structures.organic_fit: Best POV day-in-the-life fit. The owner's wife or accountant notices the quiet phone or the 14 missed calls before he does. A fellow business owner explains what he changed. Buyer pains are shown, then the mechanism is revealed. CTA: 'send this to a business owner who does this'.

story_structures.name: The viewer is the exhibit
story_structures.shape: Future or past setting → the viewer's present on display → mockery by kids or visitors → a guide gives the cause → the product in the next room
story_structures.organic_fit: 'The 2035 museum of Albanian ads': kids laugh at a wall of 'cilësi dhe çmime të mira' posts while a guide explains why everyone sounding the same forced price wars. Shareable comedy that teaches the cause. CTA: follow for part 2 / comment keyword. Low lip-sync need.

story_structures.name: The old-school archetype
story_structures.shape: Four 1 s shots of the modern routine → the archetype does easily what the modern man can't, with one-word answers → the cause in the archetype's mouth → the archetype approves the product
story_structures.organic_fit: A grandfather craftsman who sold by one sentence of reputation, beside the grandson drowning in boosted posts. Fits Albanian family-business identity. Organic close: the grandfather's one line becomes the save-worthy lesson; no offer.

story_structures.name: The family dare
story_structures.shape: A kid challenges a parent in front of the family with a stake named in the first 6 s → comic wrong answers in quick close-ups → a silent stretch of research → the kid teaches the cause → the payoff
story_structures.organic_fit: A daughter dares her father to name one thing only his ads say (the seed of 'The Bet'). Teaches a fact (sameness leads to price comparison) through a game. CTA: 'comment your one thing' drives comments, a native organic signal.

story_structures.name: The old habit as a person
story_structures.shape: The competitor or routine played as a partner → the relationship sours → a breakup scene → the new partner (the product)
story_structures.organic_fit: The '€400 a month for likes' habit, or the boost button, played as a clingy ex. Comedy works organically. Must not depict a real competitor. The skill bars it from leading a paid first test; organically it can be a series episode.

story_structures.name: Dramatic irony
story_structures.shape: Side characters mock the hero, thinking she doesn't understand → the viewer knows more → one calm line flips it → power reversal
story_structures.organic_fit: Competitors at a café mock the owner's 'lucky' full calendar; he calmly answers with the mechanism line. Strong for B2B status and pride. CTA: save/follow; the flip line becomes the caption hook.

story_structures.name: The villain's point of view
story_structures.shape: The problem itself narrates → it wins and wins → it fails because of the product → it finds the product (usually stylized, produced in readymerce-animation-ads)
story_structures.organic_fit: The 'Sa kushton?' DM as a narrator who kills every sale until it meets a post that already answered why this shop is different. Animated, so no lip-sync risk and cheap. CTA: comment keyword.

story_structures.name: The moral dilemma
story_structures.shape: A situation viewers argue about → an authority reverses the expected judgment → tied to the product's identity promise
story_structures.organic_fit: 'Should he drop the price a third time to keep the client?' Built for comments and reach, which is an organic goal. The skill bans it as a paid first test; organically it is a good engagement post with 'comment YES/NO'.

story_structures.name: The quiet monologue
story_structures.shape: One voice on a universal feeling over lived moments → no dialogue lip-sync → a soft product presence
story_structures.organic_fit: The owner's voice over night quotes, the marker, the empty phone, then the morning he stops dropping his price. Cheapest to produce (voiceover plus silent shots). Very savable and shareable for founders. CTA: 'send to someone who needs this'.

story_structures.name: Fall, then rebuild
story_structures.shape: The worst moment → the decision → the win, seen through the doubter's eyes
story_structures.organic_fit: A client case study as drama: the month he almost closed, the decision, the turnaround told through his daughter's eyes. Needs real documented facts. Good for a series. CTA: follow for the next client story.

story_structures.name: The secret plan / the bet
story_structures.shape: The viewer is let in on a plan or bet in the first seconds (bribe, dare, hidden motive) → it plays out → rule-of-three escalation → backfire or payoff → a last line that flips power
story_structures.organic_fit: The skill calls it 'strong for B2B and services, because a bet turns an argument into a game'. 'The Bet' (Era vs Arben, StraightScale) is a ready organic POV story: the owner's pain (dropping the price), the bet, the reveal that his customers fear delays, not price. Drop the price/offer close and end on 'Çmimi s'ulet' plus a comment-keyword CTA.

story_structures.name: The misjudgment
story_structures.shape: The viewer judges a character (lazy, rude, wasting money) → the reveal that they were wrong → the product is the reason
story_structures.organic_fit: We see an owner on his phone at his kid's dinner and judge him, then learn the phone is answering leads for him while he is present. Teaches the mechanism through surprise. CTA: save/share.

story_structures.name: Drama beat sheet (S90 timings)
story_structures.shape: 1 question opening (0 to 4 s) → 2 geography and want (4 to 10) → 3 friction, stakes, clock (8 to 25) → 4 turn 1 (15 to 30) → 5 search and the cause line (25 to 45) → 6 low point (40 to 55) → 7 product as the answer (45 to 75, never before 40%) → 8 mechanism and proof → 9 payoff on a face → 10 conversion and offer (70 to 80) → 11 CTA, identity close, button and end card
story_structures.organic_fit: The backbone for an organic POV reel: keep beats 1 to 9 and 11. Delete beat 10 (price, guarantee, scarcity). Compress to 30 to 45 s (C45 shape: question, geography, friction, turn with the mechanism carried in, payoff on a face, organic CTA). The mechanism reveal is the value and stays.

story_structures.name: Emotional shapes
story_structures.shape: Man in a hole (down, then up) by default; Cinderella from 60 s up; never end falling
story_structures.organic_fit: Use Man in a hole for 20 to 45 s organic reels: pain-down for 60%, the insight turn, ending higher than the start. Cinderella for longer series episodes.

story_structures.name: The snowball (reference reel, 25 s, 8 shots)
story_structures.shape: The viewer is let in on the plan (two-shot in depth) → the plan executes → the apology/meet → rule-of-three escalation (one snowball, many, kids demand money) → the planted object pays off → a last line that flips power
story_structures.organic_fit: Ideal organic length and density (8 shots at about 3.1 s, variety from size, depth and staging, few lip-sync shots). Template for a 25 s agency skit with a planted object (a flyer, a price sheet). Music out during setup and comedy, in on the emotional beat.

story_structures.name: The card in the book (reference reel, 30 s)
story_structures.shape: Start in motion → a fast collision montage (6 cuts in 1.2 s) → one hero close-up → a long depth take where a background entrance is the obstacle → an insert reveals the hidden plant → an ambiguous open last beat
story_structures.organic_fit: The open last beat 'drives comments' and part-2 asks, which are native organic signals. Template for a 30 s story whose last insert reveals what the agency changed (a new ad line on the phone), ending unresolved for an episode series.

story_structures.name: The Missed Call (worked example, 45 s)
story_structures.shape: Sound-first hook (phone buzzing on a bench, 3 shots in 3 s, no music) → partner finds 14 missed calls → argument in short lines → lost-lead insert → low point and confession ('I can't do this alone') with silence → touch and resolution cue → time cut by pre-lap and match cut to morning → answering calls, bookings insert (the product), a van loaded → payoff on her face → button joke → end card
story_structures.organic_fit: The closest ready-made POV day-in-the-life of the buyer: a furniture-workshop owner in Tirana with his pains, then the mechanism (a system that answers leads) revealed through a time cut. Swap the end card offer for 'comment CALLS' or 'follow for part 2'. 24 shots at about 1.9 s; about 40% listener time.

story_structures.name: The 8-shot dialogue template (vertical, 6 lines, about 20 s)
story_structures.shape: 1 medium-wide geography, slow push → 2 OTS on A, lip-synced → 3 B reaction (A's line over him) → 4 ECU key-object insert with rack focus, B's line J-cut → 5 B MCU low angle with orbit + Sync 3 → 6 A reaction, silence → 7 A close-up push, the turn line → 8 wide, A leaves, B's last line off-screen + door
story_structures.organic_fit: A reusable building block for a 20 s organic scene: only 3 visible lip-sync shots, so cheap and low-risk. Good for a weekly episodic format with recurring characters (series cast file, section 18).

story_structures.name: Slow burn (restraint)
story_structures.shape: Top-down phone insert → wide entrance freeze → MCU short-sided creep → matched MCU swallow → CU slides the evidence → insert stops at hand → CU high short-sided, mouth opens with nothing (turn) → wide pull-back aftermath
story_structures.organic_fit: A treatment option for a tense founder moment (an unpaid invoice, a bad review). 8 shots, minimal dialogue, cheap. The evidence insert is the 'proof on screen' rule.

story_structures.name: Emotional reveal (start close, then reveal)
story_structures.shape: ECU eyes → CU hearing the door → entrance gimbal follow → OTS eyes lift → CU question → tilt-down reveal of the object → rack focus to his face (turn) → high wide sit-down → profile two-shot
story_structures.organic_fit: A hook pattern for organic: open on a face receiving something unseen; the reveal object is the client's real problem (a stack of unanswered DMs).

story_structures.name: Confrontation (handheld, line cross at the turn)
story_structures.shape: Mid-shout CU entering → depth two-shot, back turned → OTS profile → clean single push → hand-stops insert → 90-degree arc across the line (turn) → low CU → high CU → locked profile silence → walk-out wide
story_structures.organic_fit: High-energy hook for business partners arguing over the marketing budget. Use sparingly organically; the comment test (who is right?) drives replies.

story_structures.name: Comic beat (the confrontation that deflates)
story_structures.shape: Centered symmetric wide → creep-in freeze → quick push 'Explain.' → darting eyes → insert → long excuse → whip to raised eyebrow → whip back reveal (turn) → shared symmetric wide
story_structures.organic_fit: The most organic-native: high-key, static, symmetric comedy that is cheap to generate (few moves, short lines). Good for weekly relatable-pain skits for SME owners.

story_structures.name: Quiet decision (internal)
story_structures.shape: ECU fidget (ring) → high wide through the doorway → MCU slow 45-degree orbit → rack focus to the other person and back → CU still eyes, small nod (turn) → insert object set down → stand with pedestal → silhouette exit
story_structures.organic_fit: Dialogue-free, so no lip-sync cost. For a T10-style founder reel: the night he decides to stop competing on price. Pair with captions or a VO line.

story_structures.name: Opening types (7.2)

visual_qa_overlap: What the skill already does: (1) A set bible with an identity rule. Identity comes only from the location master plus character sheets, never frame-from-frame, with one match-on-action hop allowed (8.2). (2) Frame QA on every storyboard frame (8.3.4): 12 checks covering identity vs sheet, screen side and eyeline, light source, prop hand, extra fingers, bottom 35%, spelled text, the size asked for, bleed-in characters from the master, the continuity state, the product's person not facing the lens, and adjacent frames of the same person visibly different. Plus the composition-bleed rule (crop the master for inserts). (3) The animatic review against the shot-list rules, watched on mute and eyes closed (9). (4) A prompt template per shot row with fixed order and rules (11.2: one move, end states, 2 to 5 negatives, restraint words, gesture-word ban, Kling under 300 words, Omni 1 to 2 sentences, Veo positive exclusions), plus phrase banks and anchor lines reused verbatim. (5) Per-take QA (11.6): a frame sheet at 0.5 s / 1 s plus first and last frames; checks for face vs sheet, morphing, eyeline, move obeyed, text artifacts, frozen; audio cross-correlation lag and transcript for lip-sync; a generation log. (6) Film test (16): a 1 fps frame sheet plus cut frames; shot, opening, story, sound and music audits; a continuity audit of last-frame vs first-frame at each cut; an automatic jump-cut scan (90x160 grey correlation above about 0.6); a phone shadow-floor luma check; and the 100-point score card. Fresh agents are already used for the two script cold reads (5.4). For the film, 'For high-stakes work' only, a fresh agent runs checks 2 to 6 on the frame sheet and audio tables. Gaps a fresh-agent Visual / Prompt / Take Reviewer would fill: the same agent currently generates and grades every frame, prompt and take (self-review, which is how 'The Bet' scored 68/100 with continuity breaks). A Prompt Reviewer should lint each prompt against its shot-list row before any credit is spent: continuity-state words present, anchor line verbatim, reference jobs stated, one move with an end state, negatives 2 to 5, per-model limits (no audio_references with start_image on H3; clip = stem + 1 s and 15 s or less; ~20 words; declined_preset_id handling), and banned emotion and gesture words. A Visual Reviewer should run the 8.3.4 checklist on frames at full size, including the adjacent-frame comparison, which the skill admits image models ignore ('close-up, 85mm' vs 'medium close-up, 50mm'). It should also check 9:16 safe zones with overlays, because the skill's numbers (14% top, 35 to 40% bottom, right 21% lower half, captions 55 to 62%) are only described, with no overlay tool. A Take Reviewer should independently re-run per-take QA (frame sheet, morph and hand checks, lag and correlation, transcript) and the post-edit neighbour or jump-cut re-check after every edit change (14.9b), which today depends on the editor remembering. Also needed: helper scripts for the frame sheets, correlation, jump-cut scan, loudness tables and luma floor, since the skill ships none.
